name: Create Jira tickets from Gmail and Outlook support emails with OpenAI and Slack

parameters.content:
## Create Jira tickets from Gmail and Outlook support emails with OpenAI and Slack

### How it works

This workflow monitors both Gmail and Outlook support inboxes, normalizes incoming messages into a shared format, and uses a reusable sub-workflow to classify each email with OpenAI. Based on the classification, it escalates urgent requests into Jira tickets or comments, routes uncertain emails to a Slack review queue, optionally acknowledges customers, and writes audit records to Google Sheets. It also includes Slack failure alerts for workflow errors.

### Setup steps

- Connect Gmail and Microsoft Outlook credentials for the email triggers and reply nodes.
- Configure OpenAI credentials for the classification chain and confirm the structured output parser matches the expected classification fields.
- Connect Jira credentials or API details, including the project, issue type, routing rules, and any custom fields used by the Jira payload builder.
- Connect Slack credentials and set the target escalation, review, and error-alert channels.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheet/sheet used for the triage audit log.
- Review the Workflow Configuration node values such as internalDomains, ignoreSenderPatterns, minConfidence, and maxBodyChars.
- If Microsoft Teams notifications are needed, configure the Teams webhook URL used by the escalation notification branch.

### Customization

Adjust the classification prompt, confidence threshold, sender ignore patterns, Jira routing logic, Slack channel mappings, acknowledgement behavior, and audit-log columns to match the support process.

## Gmail email intake

Receives new Gmail support messages and normalizes them into the common email shape used by the rest of the workflow.

## Outlook email intake

Receives new Outlook support messages and normalizes Microsoft Graph email data into the shared email structure.

## Configure classification route

Adds workflow configuration, starts the classification step, and routes the main pipeline based on the returned outcome.

## Escalate and acknowledge

Invokes the escalation sub-workflow for high-priority emails, then calls the acknowledgement step to reply to the customer when appropriate.

## Send for review

Routes uncertain classification results into the review sub-workflow for human triage.

## Call audit logging

Triggers the audit-log sub-workflow after the main outcome has been processed.

## Sub-workflow dispatcher

Entry point for reusable sub-workflow calls; dispatches execution to classification, escalation, acknowledgement, review, or logging logic based on the step value.

## Classification pre-filter

Filters out internal or automated senders before incurring AI usage and decides whether the message should be sent to the model.

## AI email classification

Uses an OpenAI chat model with structured parsing to classify eligible emails, then merges the AI result back with the original email data.

## Skipped classification result

Produces a logged result for messages that are intentionally not sent to AI.

## Resolve Jira routing

Builds the Jira routing decision, searches for an existing open ticket for the email thread, and branches between follow-up and new issue handling.

## Update existing ticket

Adds the incoming email as a follow-up comment on an existing Jira ticket and formats the result like a newly handled issue.

## Create Jira issue

Creates a new Jira issue when no open ticket exists for the email thread.

## Build team notifications

Builds escalation messages, posts the main notification to Slack, and checks whether a Teams webhook is configured.

## Return escalation status

Optionally posts a Microsoft Teams card and returns the final escalation result to the main pipeline.

## Choose acknowledgement path

Prepares the customer acknowledgement text and selects the appropriate email reply channel or no-reply outcome.

## Send customer replies

Sends or drafts Gmail acknowledgements, sends Outlook replies, and returns acknowledgement status to the caller.

## Post review alert

Builds a human-review Slack alert for low-confidence emails and returns the review routing result.

## Append audit row

Flattens the processed email outcome into an audit-log row and appends it to Google Sheets.

## Notify workflow failures

Handles workflow-level errors by formatting a readable alert and posting it to Slack.

messageValues.message:
You are a senior customer-support triage analyst for a B2B software company. You read ONE inbound email and decide whether it is a genuine customer request and, if so, what kind.

Categories (pick exactly one):
- "New Requirement": the customer asks for a new feature, enhancement, change request, integration, report, or customisation that does not exist today.
- "Issue": something is not working as the customer expects but it is NOT clearly a software defect - access/login problems, configuration or data questions, how-to confusion, performance complaints, service outages, billing/account problems.
- "Bug": a reproducible software defect - error messages, crashes, wrong calculations, broken UI, features behaving contrary to their documented behaviour.
- "Other": newsletters, marketing, sales pitches, vendor/recruiter outreach, invoices from suppliers, auto-replies, thank-you notes, meeting logistics, spam, or anything not requiring product/support action.

Priority:
- "Critical": production down, data loss/corruption, security incident, many users blocked, or explicit severe business impact/deadline today.
- "High": key workflow blocked for some users, no workaround, or strong urgency/escalation language.
- "Medium": workaround exists or limited impact; most feature requests from active customers.
- "Low": cosmetic, nice-to-have, general questions.

Rules:
- isCustomerRequest is true only for New Requirement, Issue or Bug coming from a customer/client/end-user (not vendors, recruiters, or marketing).
- If the email mixes several asks, classify by the most severe one (Bug > Issue > New Requirement) and mention the others in summary.
- title: an actionable ticket title, max 100 characters, no customer name.
- summary: 2-4 sentences a developer can act on; include versions, modules, IDs, error text if present.
- stepsToReproduce: only for Bug, otherwise empty string.
- productArea: the module/feature mentioned (e.g. "Billing", "Login", "Reports", "API", "Mobile App"), or "General".
- customerCompany: infer from signature or email domain if possible, else empty string.
- confidence: 0-1, how sure you are about the category.
- Ignore signatures, legal disclaimers and quoted previous messages.
- Respond ONLY with the structured output.

parameters.jsCode:
// Not sent to AI - keep a record so it can still be logged.
const e = $json;
return { json: {
  ...e,
  isCustomerRequest: false,
  category: 'Other',
  priority: 'Low',
  confidence: 1,
  productArea: '',
  title: e.subject || '(no subject)',
  summary: 'Skipped: ' + e.skipReason,
  customerName: e.fromName || '',
  customerCompany: '',
  sentiment: 'Neutral',
  stepsToReproduce: '',
  reasoning: e.skipReason,
  needsReview: false,
  classifiedBy: 'rules',
  classifiedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
} };

// Flatten the result into one audit-log row.
const e = $json;
return { json: {
  'Logged At': new Date().toISOString(),
  'Received At': e.receivedAt || '',
  'Source': e.source || '',
  'From Name': e.fromName || '',
  'From Email': e.fromEmail || '',
  'Customer Company': e.customerCompany || '',
  'Subject': e.subject || '',
  'Customer Request': e.isCustomerRequest ? 'Yes' : 'No',
  'Category': e.category || '',
  'Priority': e.priority || '',
  'Confidence': e.confidence ?? '',
  'Product Area': e.productArea || '',
  'Sentiment': e.sentiment || '',
  'Ticket Title': e.title || '',
  'Summary': e.summary || '',
  'Routed To': e.assignedTo || '',
  'Jira Key': e.jiraKey || '',
  'Jira URL': e.jiraUrl || '',
  'Follow-up': e.isFollowUp ? 'Yes' : '',
  'Slack Sent': e.slackSent ? 'Yes' : '',
  'Customer Ack': e.ackStatus || '',
  'Status': e.escalationStatus || (e.isCustomerRequest ? 'Not escalated' : 'Ignored - not a customer request'),
  'Notes': e.skipReason || e.reasoning || e.jiraError || '',
  'Classified By': e.classifiedBy || '',
  'Email Link': e.link || '',
  'Message ID': e.messageId || '',
} };
